content:
Jordan Lee  1721865508
Kicking off a thread on policy guardrails for overload fallback/degradation configs. We’re seeing a few “clever” configs in staging that can create infinite loops / retry storms.

Concrete example:
- primary: `model=A` in `us-east`
- fallback chain: `model=B` in `us-west` -> fallback back to `model=A` in `us-east` (because “prefer cheapest”) and clients retry on 503

If breakers open, this can bounce forever (or until TTL) and amplify load. We need something deterministic + safe.

Benji Okafor  1721865631
:+1: We should treat customer-provided policy as *input*, not gospel.

Proposal sketch:
1) Validate config at write-time (Console/API) with a “policy linter”
2) Enforce runtime guardrails even if config slipped through (max hops, cycle detection)

For (2), we can add headers / response fields so customers can debug why fallback didn’t happen.

Mina Haddad  1721865744
Agree. Routing is currently “best effort” applying fallback list; it doesn’t prevent a loop if the list repeats (esp with “region preference” rules).

We also need to decide where enforcement lives:
- policy engine (Jordan’s service)
- routing service (closest to execution)
- gateway (edge) to stop crazy client retries

My vote: policy engine validates + routing enforces hop cap.

Ravi Menon  1721865902
What’s the desired behavior when fallback list contains a cycle?

Option A: reject config (hard fail at config write)
Option B: accept but routing short-circuits (drops repeated destinations)

I like A for explicitness, but we’ll need a migration story since a bunch of internal templates already do “fallback to primary after 30s” style (not a strict cycle but can look like one).

Elena Popov  1721866048
We should separate “fallback” (alternate destination) vs “retry after cooldown” (same destination later).

A lot of these configs are trying to express: “if us-east is brown, try us-west; when us-east recovers, resume.” That’s not a fallback loop, it’s normal recovery. But the *policy graph* can still look cyclic.

Maybe the guardrail is: during a single request, no destination can be visited twice. That handles the per-request infinite loop case.

Then config validation can allow cycles if they require a time condition / breaker cooldown boundary.

Peter Holtz  1721866203
From SRE side: per-request hop cap is mandatory.

We’ve already seen chain amplification:
- routing does A->B->C
- each hop triggers a control-plane lookup + capacity signal fetch
- under load, that extra traffic can push control-plane into the red :grimacing:

So even without cycles, a long chain is bad.

Suggest:
- max_fallback_hops = 2 (maybe 3) for Hosted
- dedicated can be different but we should default low

Brian Murphy  1721866356
Also, customer-facing error semantics: if we stop fallback due to guardrail, we need a stable error code.

E.g. `overload_policy_violation` or `overload_fallback_exhausted`.

We *should not* return a generic 500 when guardrails trigger.

Amara Diallo  1721866501
Gateway angle: if customers have “retry on 503 forever” behavior, we’re going to get hammered even with perfect routing.

But I agree guardrails belong server-side. At gateway we can add a “don’t retry me” hint too:
- for certain overload codes, set `Retry-After` + maybe `X-Redwood-Retry-Policy: backoff`

(We’re already doing `Retry-After` for 429/503; just need consistent semantics.)

Christine Wong  1721866620
On breaker integration: if fallback chain keeps trying destinations that are open-breaker, it’s basically tight-looping inside our system.

We can short-circuit earlier:
- routing evaluates candidates and filters any with breaker=open
- if all candidates are open, return immediately with overload-protected error

This is also good for “unsafe” configs that list only saturated pools.

Jordan Lee  1721866798
Synthesizing:

Runtime enforcement (request-time):
- per-request “visited set” of (model, region, tier)
- max hops
- filter breaker=open candidates before selection
- if guardrail triggers, return stable overload error w/ reason

Config-time linting:
- detect pure cycles in fallback graph without time/breaker boundary
- warn/error on hop-length > N
- warn if fallback target is same tier/region w/ no change (often misconfig)

Question: where to store “visited set” so it’s consistent across gateway->routing? Would prefer routing owns it and gateway only passes initial attributes.

Ravi Menon  1721867012
Visited set can live in routing request context. But for OpenAI-compat streaming, we need to be careful not to retry/fallback mid-stream.

Rule should be:
- fallback only before first token (prefill)
- once streaming starts, no server-side fallback; if disconnect happens, client retries with `Retry-After`

So hop cap mostly applies to prefill routing stage.

Mina Haddad  1721867180
Yes. Streaming fallback mid-response is a correctness nightmare (partial outputs). We should document: “no mid-stream fallback; you may see disconnect/503.”

For non-streaming: routing can do one internal re-route before execution.

Benji Okafor  1721867328
Implementation idea:
- policy engine emits a compiled “candidate list” with metadata per step (priority, constraints)
- routing evaluates candidates in order, applying:
  - breaker filtering
  - visited-set filtering
  - hop cap

If candidates exhausted -> return overload error with `reason=fallback_exhausted` + include `attempted=[...]` but keep it bounded (cardinality/log size).

We also need to prevent “fallback to cheaper tier” loops (standard->basic->standard). Might be easiest to treat (tier) as part of the visited key.

Peter Holtz  1721867519
Please keep attempted list out of metrics labels. We can log it (sampled) but metrics should have coarse labels only.

Also add a trace event when guardrail triggers:
`overload.policy.guardrail_triggered=true`
`overload.policy.guardrail_reason=cycle_detected|hop_cap|breaker_open_all`

Elena Popov  1721867706
One more unsafe pattern: customers config fallback to *same* destination but different “variant” (quantization profile) and it oscillates.

E.g. q8 -> q4 -> q8 based on latency threshold. That’s a loop too.

We should include “variant” (or runtime profile) in the visited set if variant fallback is supported.

Brian Murphy  1721867904
Naming + customer docs:
- “fallback_exhausted” implies we tried what we could, safe failure
- “policy_invalid” for config-time rejection
- “policy_guardrail_triggered” for request-time short-circuit (but might sound scary)

I’d prefer:
- config: 400 w/ `invalid_policy`
- request-time: 503 w/ `overloaded` + `subcode=fallback_exhausted` or `subcode=guardrail`

But ADR-0147 has the canonical mapping; we should align. (linking here: https://confluence.redwood/arch/decision-records/adr-0147)

Christine Wong  1721868059
ADR-0147 currently has `overload_shed` reasons like `capacity_exhausted`, `queue_full`, `breaker_open`.

Maybe we add `policy_guardrail` as a shed reason? That would keep it in the same taxonomy.

Jordan Lee  1721868266
I like `policy_guardrail` as a shed reason (fits “safe deterministic shedding”).

Action items I’ll take:
1) Add to policy engine spec: compile-time validator + cycle detection rules (w/ exception for “recovery” style cycles)
2) Routing: implement visited-set + hop cap + breaker filtering (Mina/Ravi, can we slot this into ENG-4838?)
3) Error semantics: Brian/Christine sync on naming in ADR-0147 + OpenAI-compat mapping

Benji Okafor  1721868413
Re: cycle detection exception — we should be crisp. Something like:
- cycle allowed only if it includes a “wait” boundary (cooldown) that can’t happen within a single request

But since we don’t have “wait” inside the router, per-request visited-set already prevents that being an actual loop.

So config-time: downgrade cycles to WARN not ERROR, unless hop count > N or destination repeats in direct list.

Mina Haddad  1721868617
:+1: warn is safer to avoid blocking legit “resume primary when healthy” configs.

For routing enforcement, we can implement without depending on policy engine changes.

Ravi Menon  1721868803
I’ll open a small PR in routing service to add:
- `max_hops` default 2
- `visited` set key = model+region+tier (+variant if present)
- early stop when exhausted

We’ll need to make sure this is feature-flagged per region/model like the rest of overload protection.

Amara Diallo  1721869054
When routing returns `policy_guardrail` shed reason, gateway should map to consistent HTTP + headers.

If it’s 503, we should set `Retry-After` to something non-zero (maybe same as breaker cooldown?). Otherwise clients will hot-loop.

Jordan Lee  1721869310
Good point. We can reuse “recommended_retry_after_seconds” field from router response to gateway.

Also, we should add a Console UX note (DES-207?) to surface policy warnings: “Your fallback policy contains cycles; router will not revisit destinations within a request.”

Peter Holtz  1721869588
Please make sure oncall has a way to see when guardrails are firing at scale. Dashboard panel:
- % of shed reasons = policy_guardrail by region/model/tier

If it spikes, it might indicate a bad template rollout.

Brian Murphy  1721869920
One more compat nit: OpenAI clients sometimes treat 429 differently than 503.

If guardrail is not strictly “rate limit,” keep it 503. For 429 we want “you exceeded quota / too many requests.”

So 503 + Retry-After seems right.

Christine Wong  1721870147
Agreed. We should avoid turning policy guardrails into 429 because customers will assume “raise limits” solves it.

This is “we can’t safely route you right now.”

Elena Popov  1721870529
Ok. Also consider: if a customer configured fallback to a different region but disallowed cross-region by compliance flag, we should fail fast w/ a clear reason.

That’s not overload, but it’s still a “policy guardrail” block.

Jordan Lee  1721870894
Yeah, guardrails isn’t only overload. But for now, this thread is overload-related; compliance blocks should be `invalid_policy` at config-time ideally.

If it’s dynamic (e.g. compliance changes), then request-time would return something else (probably 403). Let’s keep scope limited.

Benji Okafor  1721871342
Can we document the hard limits somewhere?
- max_hops
- no revisit per request
- no mid-stream fallback

So Support/CS can point to a canonical doc instead of tribal knowledge.

Jordan Lee  1721872146
Yep. I’ll add a section to the internal policy spec + ping Elliot/Wei for docs once we land the behavior. Thanks all.
